items.statement: For full-column-rank X∈R^{n×p} with p<n, an error-contrast matrix is K∈R^{n×(n-p)} of full column rank with X^T K=0 and columns spanning col(X)^⊥.

items.statement: For a fixed-design first-moment model with full-column-rank X and known positive-definite covariance V, define βhat_GLS=(X^T V^{-1}X)^{-1}X^T V^{-1}Y as the Borel-measurable estimator of β.

items.title: Finite-dimensional linear mixed model with explicit longitudinal roles
items.statement: On a declared probability space, let fixed matrices X and Z define Y=Xβ+Zb+ε, with finite second moments, Eb=Eε=0, Cov(b)=G, Cov(ε)=R, and b independent of ε. Specify subject and visit roles, observed visit sets, and the separately declared missingness mechanism. No Gaussian or ignorability assumption is included.
items.strategy: Define the finite-dimensional moment model and its scientific record; keep visit indexing and the observation mechanism explicit.

items.title: Gaussian branch of the linear mixed model
items.statement: The Gaussian branch assumes AC and that the concatenated latent and residual vector (b, ε) is multivariate normal with mean zero and covariance diag(G,R); it is an explicit additional assumption, separate from the moment-only mixed model.
items.strategy: Declare the joint Gaussian submodel and its inherited AC assumption without imposing Gaussianity on the moment-only branch.

items.title: Longitudinal observation patterns and missingness mechanisms
items.statement: A longitudinal missingness mechanism assigns each finite observation pattern a nonnegative probability summing to one at every full-response and covariate state, with each pattern probability measurable. MCAR is outcome-independent, MAR depends on outcomes only through observed coordinates, and MNAR is failure of MAR on declared support. Monotone dropout observes an initial segment of visits.
items.strategy: Define full and observed response records, pattern indicators, and MCAR/MAR/MNAR relative to a declared observation kernel.

items.title: A mixed-model covariance does not imply MAR dropout
items.statement: It is false that a correct random-intercept covariance model for a complete two-visit response vector implies dropout after the first visit is missing at random (MAR).

items.title: Random-intercept covariance and intraclass correlation
items.statement: For independent mean-zero random intercept b_j and residuals ε_ij with variances τ² and σ², two observations from the same subject have covariance τ², marginal variance τ²+σ², and correlation τ²/(τ²+σ²) when the denominator is positive.
